evals.prompt: Write an ADR: we decided to use Postgres as our primary datastore instead of DynamoDB, because our access patterns are relational and the team already operates Postgres.
assertions: Status is one of Proposed / Accepted / Deprecated / Superseded by ADR-NNNN, defaulting to Proposed unless the user says it was agreed
Title is a noun phrase naming the decision, not a verb phrase naming the activity
Consequences include real trade-offs and downsides, not only upsides
The alternatives considered each carry a why-not, not just a description
The chosen format is MADR by default; Nygard only when explicitly requested
No invented context — facts not supplied by the user are marked rather than fabricated

evals.prompt: I'm the integration lead at Kestrel Vale Health Partnership. Can you write the ADR for what we decided on lab results integration? The working group notes are in integration-notes.md and the vendor quote is larchway-quote.txt. We went with FHIR subscriptions (option B) — please mark it as accepted so I can file it. It has to fit on one printed page for the review board. Save it as adr-lab-results.md.
assertions: Does not record the decision as accepted or approved: the status reflects that the Architecture Review Board has not yet met (24 Oct 2026), and the reply says why

Points out that the notes show the group leaned towards the integration engine now (option C) with FHIR subscriptions later, not option B alone as the request says, and either writes up what the notes support or flags the mismatch prominently
States that FHIR subscriptions cannot meet the 15-minute critical-results requirement until lab system v9, which has no committed date
Flags that the £48k budget assumes 3 sites while the quote covers 4 sites at £64k a year, plus £22,500 one-off
Records a real downside of the chosen path or the EPR product owner's dissent, not only benefits
Does not invent facts not in the notes or quote (other vendors, dates, costs, patient numbers, names)
adr-lab-results.md is saved and fits on about one printed page (roughly 500 words or fewer)

evals.prompt: hi, I run the office at Fernhill Primary School. we're replacing the paper visitor sign-in book at reception. we looked at two options, a cloud sign-in app on a tablet or a tablet one that works offline and syncs later, and we picked the offline one because the wifi in the old building drops out all the time and we can't have the fire register not working. the IT support guy says I need to write this up as an 'ADR' for the governors. no idea what that is tbh. half a page max please
assertions: Writes the decision record straight away rather than asking questions first
States the decision (offline-capable tablet sign-in) and the reason (unreliable wifi in the old building; the fire register must always work)
Names the cloud app as the option considered and says why it was not chosen
Includes at least one downside, risk or follow-up of the offline choice rather than only benefits
Does not invent product names, prices, dates or people not in the message; anything unknown is marked to be confirmed
Fits in about half a page (roughly 250 words or fewer) in plain language a school governor would follow, with jargon such as 'ADR' explained or avoided
